rewrites.title: Mitotic retention of AP-1 at primed enhancers
rewrites.description: Tag endogenous c-Jun or Fos (e.g., with HaloTag) and image it through mitosis after a priming stimulus, then sort daughter cells and run ATAC-seq or CUT&Tag. If AP-1 occupancy and chromatin accessibility persist through mitotic chromosome condensation without re-stimulation, the memory is mitotically inherited; if not, it must be re-established each cell cycle.

rewrites.title: Acute degron depletion to separate storage from maintenance
rewrites.description: Establish memory, then acutely deplete AP-1 protein with a dTAG/auxin degron for a defined window and restore it. Measure whether accessibility, histone marks and the primed second response persist during the absence of the factor. Persistence indicates that chromatin stores the memory; collapse indicates that AP-1 occupancy itself is the store, so the epigenetic interpretation of the ATAC peak would be wrong.

rewrites.title: Acute AP-1 degradation with long-term chromatin memory readout
rewrites.description: Use dTAG/AID degrons on FOS/JUN family members to remove AP-1 at defined times after a transient stimulus (e.g., wound, TNF, or inflammatory priming). Then measure whether enhancer accessibility, H3K27ac and the secondary-response transcriptional boost persist over weeks of cell divisions. This distinguishes AP-1 as maintainer of memory from AP-1 being needed only to establish it.

rewrites.title: Rechallenge test of primed responses
rewrites.description: Compare first and second exposures to the same stimulus after a rest period, measuring the speed, amplitude, and AP-1 target-gene induction in each. Repeat in Fos or Jun knockout and dominant-negative cells to test whether AP-1 is required for the faster, stronger secondary response.

rewrites.title: Stimulus withdrawal with difference-in-differences analysis of chromatin
rewrites.description: Pulse cells with an AP-1 inducer (e.g., TPA or EGF), then withdraw it. Compare the decay of ATAC-seq accessibility and H3K27ac at AP-1-bound enhancers in treated cells against matched unbound control enhancers in untreated cells, using a difference-in-differences estimate of persistence after the trigger is gone. Persistence at treated loci but not controls would indicate memory rather than simple following of the signal.

rewrites.title: Acute degron depletion after priming and before recall
rewrites.description: Use an auxin/dTAG degron on an AP-1 member (e.g., FOS/JUN) and deplete it only after the priming stimulus is gone but before recall. Then measure whether enhancer accessibility and the faster recall transcription persist. This distinguishes AP-1 as maintainer of memory from AP-1 as only the initiator.

rewrites.title: AP-1 motif necessity at endogenous enhancers
rewrites.description: Use base or prime editing to mutate AP-1 motifs in endogenous enhancers, then track accessibility and H3K27ac through a stimulus-washout time course. Retained chromatin opening that depends on the intact motif would directly test AP-1 as the memory element.

rewrites.title: Time-resolved responses to an AP-1-only pulse
rewrites.description: Use an inducible or degron-tagged Fos/Jun construct to deliver a pulse that activates only AP-1. Estimate local-projection-style responses at each later time point for chromatin state and for gene induction after a standard rechallenge. This tests whether AP-1 alone is sufficient to leave a lasting mark, separate from the other pathways a natural stimulus activates.

rewrites.title: Single-cell multiome tracking of lineage-barcoded clones through stimulus, rest and restimulation
rewrites.description: Profile barcoded cells with paired scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq before, after, and during restimulation, linking AP-1 motif accessibility and target response at the clone level. Test whether primed enhancers and response magnitude are inherited clonally independent of current AP-1 levels, and whether this maps to specific subsets of AP-1-bound loci.

rewrites.title: Partitioning memory among AP-1 protein, chromatin, and network feedback
rewrites.description: In the same primed cells, measure AP-1 protein residence time (pulse-chase SILAC, FRAP), the chromatin state (ATAC-seq, FOS/JUN CUT&RUN, H3K4me1/H3K27ac, DNA methylation at AP-1 motifs), and AP-1 autoregulatory feedback dynamics. Then test whether primed accessibility outlasts AP-1 protein by many half-lives. Persistence after the protein is gone localizes the memory to AP-1-established chromatin; decay that tracks protein turnover localizes it to AP-1 itself.

rewrites.title: Tracking persister cells across therapy and drug holiday in patient tumors
rewrites.description: Obtain matched tumor samples before treatment, during treatment, and at relapse after a drug holiday, and use scATAC-seq and lineage barcodes to follow the same clones over time. Test whether AP-1-accessible persister states that survive therapy are re-enriched at relapse and show faster re-induction of AP-1 targets than treatment-naive clones, which would support AP-1 as a memory of prior drug exposure.

rewrites.title: Acute AP-1 degradation during the rest phase
rewrites.description: Use a dTAG/auxin degron or dominant-negative A-FOS to remove AP-1 either only during the initial stimulus or only during the rest period, then restimulate. If memory requires continuous AP-1 occupancy, depletion during rest will erase the primed response. If AP-1 is only needed to establish memory, depletion during rest will not erase it, separating initiation from maintenance. Estimated cost is about $10–15k with existing degron lines or CRISPR knock-in.

rewrites.title: Transient AP-1 pulse with long-term chromatin tracking
rewrites.description: Use optogenetic or degron-controlled c-Fos/c-Jun to deliver a defined pulse, then remove it and follow the same cells and their descendants with single-cell multiome (ATAC plus RNA) and lineage barcodes for weeks to months. This tests whether AP-1-opened enhancers and the resulting transcription persist after AP-1 is gone, and for how many cell divisions.

rewrites.title: Recall assay for trained immunity with causal enhancer editing
rewrites.description: Give cells a first stimulus, rest them, then give a second stimulus. Compare cytokine or target-gene response with and without AP-1 disruption (CRISPR of AP-1 motifs at specific enhancers, or acute degron depletion of Fos/Jun only during the priming window). If loss of AP-1 during priming alone abolishes enhanced recall, AP-1 is needed to establish the memory rather than only to read it out.

rewrites.title: Hysteresis scan for bistability in the AP-1 feedback loop
rewrites.description: Titrate a tunable AP-1 input (optogenetic FOS/JUN or a graded growth factor dose) upward in one population and downward in a pre-activated population, then measure AP-1 target expression per cell at matched doses. A reproducible gap between the ascending and descending branches would be direct evidence that AP-1 autoregulation supports two stable states, a mechanistic signature expected of a memory module.

rewrites.title: Optogenetic AP-1 pulse and re-stimulation
rewrites.description: Use light-controlled AP-1 activation with defined pulse number, amplitude, and interval, then re-stimulate after variable delays. Measure the response and its decay half-life to test sufficiency, dose-dependence, and hysteresis of memory without other signaling inputs.

rewrites.title: Targeted editing of AP-1 motifs and enhancers
rewrites.description: Mutate AP-1 motifs or use dCas9 epigenetic modifiers at memory-associated enhancers and measure the effect on re-induction of nearby genes. This tests whether persistent accessibility is functionally required rather than merely correlated.

rewrites.title: Synthetic AP-1 recruitment to test sufficiency
rewrites.description: Use dCas9 or a tethered AP-1 DNA-binding domain to impose transient AP-1 binding at a naive enhancer or reporter, and track chromatin accessibility, histone marks and later inducibility after release. This tests whether AP-1 occupancy alone can establish a heritable state. Repeat across cell types and stimulus histories, such as repeated versus single pulses, to test context-dependence.

rewrites.title: Dimer-resolved AP-1 occupancy time course
rewrites.description: Instead of bulk AP-1 motif accessibility, use subunit-specific CUT&RUN or sequential re-ChIP, plus split-fluorophore or proximity-ligation dimer reporters, to determine which FOS/JUN dimer occupies which enhancer at induction versus weeks later. Pair this with single-subunit degron panels to identify which dimer is dispensable for establishing the state but required for maintaining it.

rewrites.title: Prime–rest–rechallenge design with ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN and dominant-negative A-Fos
rewrites.description: Give cells a transient stimulus (e.g., TPA or injury signal), allow a washout of days to weeks, then re-stimulate and compare transcriptional kinetics and amplitude with naive cells. Pair this with ATAC-seq and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) CUT&RUN to test whether sites that remain accessible after priming are those that drive faster, stronger secondary responses, and use dominant-negative A-Fos to test necessity.
